analyzed_vuln.description: In Compiler::simplifyExpression, constructor-flattening logic keeps references to `Constructor& c = expr->as<Constructor>()` and repeatedly uses `c.type()` / `c.arguments()` after invoking helper rewrites (e.g. `delete_left`, `delete_right`, `vectorize_*`, `try_replace_expression`) elsewhere in the same optimization pass that can replace or destroy IR nodes in the current block. This allows stale expression/type pointers from the pool-backed IR to be read after they have been poisoned by ASan, surfacing as a UAF read in Type::columns(). The crash occurs at `c.type().columns()` but the root bug is unsafe lifetime/use of IR node references during in-place CFG expression simplification.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered via SkRuntimeEffect::Make on attacker-controlled SkSL source. The input must produce IR that enters scanCFG -> simplifyExpression constructor optimization and causes in-place expression rewrites in the same pass/rescan cycle, so a constructor/type reference becomes stale before `columns()` is read. The provided PoC with malformed constructor syntax (`... an(),float[](); ...` plus trailing bytes) drives this optimizer path during convertProgram/optimize, leading to read of poisoned memory from the compiler pool.
